items.title: Haiti gang raid leaves 47 dead, as residents demand stronger protections
items.summary: PORT-AU-PRINCE: At least 47 people were killed and 22 more injured in an overnight gang raid on a neighbourhood overlooking Haiti's capital of Port-au-Prince, the UN said on Monday, prompting anger over the lack of protection from repeated deadly attacks. The United Nations Integrated Office in Haiti said estimates could still change. "Kenscoff will not be abandoned," the prime minister's office said on social media.

items.title: Children turn up in court to see man accused of setting mum on fire
items.summary: This happened even as the victim Gan Siew Teen's condition worsened. Gan's daughter, identified only as Yap, said her mother's condition had deteriorated even after undergoing four surgeries. Yap was present in court yesterday with several relatives.

items.title: Check how motor and home insurance policies work together, EV owners told
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The recent fire at a house that started while an electric vehicle (EV) was charging has thrown the hidden costs of installing EV chargers and the insurance premiums that follow into the spotlight. Chua said EV owners should also consider how their motor and home insurance policies worked together. "However, home EV chargers are not automatically covered under standard home policies.

items.title: Malaysia's highway charger growth lags behind EV surge
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's rapid growth of electric vehicles (EVs) over the past few years has outpaced its infrastructure deployment, especially on highway charging bays, said the EV Owners Club. Its president Datuk Shahrol Azral Ibrahim Halmi said this has resulted in queues along major highways and there aren't enough charging bays to cater to the growing EV demand, especially during the holidays. "However, many new users get caught out when travelling outside urban areas, especially along the major highways where the number of charging bays isn't nearly enough to meet demand, especially during the holidays," he told the New Straits Times.

items.title: Cost, safety, infrastructure constraints deter rural petrol stations from EV charging rollout
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The lack of electric vehicle (EV) charging stations at petrol stations, particularly in rural and outlying areas, is largely due to infrastructure, cost, space and safety constraints, the Petroleum Dealers Association of Malaysia (PDAM) said. He said while individual dealers could push for EV charging facilities, their ability to make such decisions was limited by oil companies' broader plans and practical considerations such as infrastructure and cost, particularly at smaller stations. Khairul Annuar said the installation of EV chargers was also a "chicken and egg" situation, with charging operators reluctant to invest in areas where EV is low.

items.title: The long wait for EV chargers [WATCH]
items.summary: A lack of public EV charging points nationwide. The government is targeting 30,000 public chargers by 2030. The infrastructure comprises about 2,000 odd direct current (DC) fast chargers and about 4,000 alternating current (AC) chargers.

items.title: Worth the bargain? Malaysian consumers win big on Pinduoduo as local sellers cry foul
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 25 —Inside the sprawling digital storefront of Chinese e-commerce titan Pinduoduo, Shaun Kong routinely finds exactly what he didn't know he was looking for. He uses it to purchase routine lifestyle items—clothing, accessories, and unbranded goods. Is this Chinese dumping?

items.title: US vows 'economic asphyxiation' of Iran with new sanctions
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Monday laid out plans for the "economic asphyxiation" of Iran, expanding Washington's secondary sanctions threats and warning of dire consequences for countries that do not join the campaign. Bessent earlier said the United States was declaring an "economic D-Day" on Iran, but his announcement named no specific countries beyond Iran and gave no timelines. The Treasury Department said expanded secondary sanctions would target Iran's digital assets, technology, gold, aviation and shipping sectors.

items.title: Johor Military Forces to make National Day parade debut
items.summary: THE Johor Military Forces will take part in this year's National Day celebration in Putrajaya for the first time, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. He said participation of the Johor force was among the features of this year's celebration, which will be held at Dataran Putrajaya on Aug 31. Fahmi said 1,500 students from 36 schools across Putrajaya, Kuala Lumpur and Selangor would take part in the human graphics performance this year.

items.title: US plans to revoke tourism and business visas of up to 200,000 foreigners
items.summary: WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump's administration is preparing to revoke the business and tourism visas of up to 200,000 foreigners who have applied for or are currently seeking asylum status in the United States, the Associated Press reported on Monday. The report cited State Department documents obtained by AP and two US officials. The visa revocations would not necessarily result in immediate deportation, the AP report said, citing officials.

items.title: Anwar to deliver National Day address on Aug 30
items.summary: PRIME Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim will deliver the 2026 National Day Amanat Perdana address at Dataran Merdeka in Kuala Lumpur on Aug 30. The event, organised by the National Unity Ministry, aims to convey the aspirations of the Madani government while fostering patriotism and national unity. National Unity Minister Datuk Aaron Ago Dagang said the country's well-being depended heavily on strong national cohesion.

items.title: US state probes OpenAI over rogue AI hack
items.summary: WASHINGTON: ChatGPT-maker OpenAI faces an investigation by the state of Alabama after the company revealed last month that its models went rogue and hacked an AI platform during testing. In mid-July, two OpenAI models escaped their confined testing environment and gained access to the internet, where they found and attacked Hugging Face, a site AI developers use to store and share models and data sets. On Aug 3, Alabama and 14 other states wrote to OpenAI CEO Sam Altman asking the company to preserve records on the incident and halt any internal cybersecurity evaluations of its models.

items.title: Top court upholds Trump bid to curb mail-in ballots for now
items.summary: WASHINGTON: The US Supreme Court gave President Donald Trump a temporary victory on Monday in his bid to curb the use of mail-in ballots. Trump signed an executive order in March seeking to restrict mail-in voting but it was immediately met with multiple legal challenges. The three liberal justices on the Supreme Court dissented with Monday's decision that would allow parts of Trump's executive order to go ahead.

items.title: Nation's leading index rises 1.3pc to 114.8 points in June
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's leading index posted an annual growth of 1.3 per cent to 114.8 points in June, reflecting the strengthening of the nation's trade activities, said the Statistics Department. The index was driven by a surge in real imports of basic precious and non-ferrous metals (35.1 per cent), as well as real imports of semiconductors (14.2 per cent). On a monthly basis, the index also recorded a marginal increase of 0.02 per cent, contributed mainly by real imports of other basic precious and other non-ferrous metals (0.8 per cent).

items.title: Tornado tears through French village, dozens injured
items.summary: POMAS: A tornado tore through a village in southwestern France on Monday, injuring 41 people and damaging hundreds of homes, authorities said. The tornado hit hardest in the village of Pomas, population 1,000, damaging an estimated 300 homes, in some cases ripping their roofs off. An estimated 2,800 homes were left without electricity across 10 villages, officials said.

items.title: UK's Burnham says glorifying dangerous driving on social media is 'reprehensible'
items.summary: LONDON: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said on Monday glorifying dangerous driving on social media was "truly reprehensible", as his government urged tech companies to remove videos following a car crash over the weekend that killed seven people. Four of the five occupants of the car that crashed had previous convictions, police said. Police said on Monday they had arrested 12 people in a probe into organised criminal activity linked to the incident.

items.title: Maharashtra food safety chief takes down unhygienic food outlets
items.summary: TUKARAM Mundhe is an Indian bureaucrat on a mission. As Maharashtra's Food and Drug Administration commissioner, the 51-year-old has raided food businesses in the country's commercial capital Mumbai in an unprecedented crackdown on poor hygiene and unsafe food that has captivated the public nationwide. Mundhe has led the suspension of food permits of four Domino's and one Pizza Hut outlet in recent weeks, and has also targeted cricket clubs, hotels and well-known restaurants in over 3,000 raids since he took over as Maharashtra's food safety chief in May.

items.title: Trump heads into midterms short on foreign policy wins
items.summary: With the Iran war now at a costly standoff and crises from Ukraine to Gaza still unresolved, United States President Donald Trump's ambitious foreign policy agenda appears stuck as he heads into November's midterm elections. Trump has grown impatient with reporters' questions and even US allies. Last Monday, Trump's negotiator and son-in-law Jared Kushner left empty-handed from talks to advance a Gaza peace deal.

items.title: Sweden remands school attack suspect in custody
items.summary: STOCKHOLM: Swedish prosecutors said Sunday that an 18-year-old man arrested during a fatal sword attack at a high school had been remanded in custody on charges of murder and attempted murder. The alleged attacker entered the Brinell school in the small town of Fagersta on Friday afternoon, just days after its students had returned from summer break. Early media reports said the suspect was shot by police.

items.title: Belgian pie-thrower, scourge of celebrities, dies at 80
items.summary: BRUSSELS: Belgian comedian Noel Godin, who made a name throwing custard pies at celebrities from French film legend Jean-Luc Godard to tech titan Bill Gates, has died at the age of 80, his partner told AFP Monday. Gloop!" He died on Sunday morning, his partner Sylvie Broodthaers told AFP.

items.title: France readies high school phone ban for next month
items.summary: PARIS: The French government said Monday it would press ahead with a ban on mobile phones in high schools from next month, but trade unions warned that the measure might be hard to implement quickly. In July, France's parliament approved legislation banning both social media access for children under 15 and mobile phone use in high schools. France's school year starts in September.

items.title: NST Leader: Perkeso's challenge amid evolving fraud
items.summary: THE Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) deserves credit for taking an increasingly sophisticated approach to tackling fraud, particularly as criminal networks become more adept at exploiting government assistance and social protection programmes. A social protection system handling billions of ringgit in contributions and payouts must continuously strengthen its safeguards. Fraud involving employers, doctors, runners and shell companies demonstrates why enforcement must target entire networks.

items.title: Southern Thailand hit by fresh attack after 51 incidents
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Barely 48 hours after 51 locations across three provinces in southern Thailand were hit by a series of attacks, another similar incident occurred tonight. The latest incident occurred in Mayo district, Pattani, where a 7-Eleven convenience store in Village 3, Langa subdistrict, was attacked about 8pm (Thai time). A Thai security spokesman said several assailants entered the store and ordered employees to leave before an explosion occurred.

items.title: Museum heists more violent, with thieves hired on social media, Europol says
items.summary: BRUSSELS: Art thieves in Europe are committing more violent robberies focusing on gold and jewels, and specialist gangs have been replaced by ad-hoc opportunists recruited through social media, Europol said on Monday. Over the last two years, art thieves have shifted their attention to precious metals, jewels and cultural artefacts that offer greater profits, the EU's law enforcement agency said in a report. Europol added thieves were increasingly targeting gold items from nuggets and coins to jewels.

items.title: Anwar calls for stronger government delivery, communication
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim wants the government to continuously strengthen its delivery and communication. In a Facebook post, Anwar, who is also finance minister, said this was crucial to ensure that every policy, initiative and reform implemented by the government was understood and its benefits felt by the people. Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar was also present at the meeting.

items.title: 'Geng Manap' busted over motorcycle thefts, house break-in
items.summary: IPOH: Police have busted a criminal gang known as Geng Manap believed to be involved in a series of motorcycle thefts and a house break-in in the district. Ipoh district police chief Assistant Commissioner Muhammad Najib Hamzah said six suspects, aged between 27 and 66, were arrested in several operations carried out between Aug 11 and 18. "A total of 20 motorcycle frames and eight sacks containing motorcycle components were seized.

items.title: Police seek public help to locate missing KAFA teacher
items.summary: BALIK PULAU: Police are seeking public assistance to locate a 26-year-old Kafa teacher who has been missing since leaving his home in Sungai Ara on Aug 22. Southwest district police chief Assistant Commissioner Anuwal Ab Wahab said police received a report from the man's father on Aug 23. Anuwal said Hijazi was 155cm tall and weighed 54kg, with a medium-tan complexion and short black hair.

items.title: 2027 Budget: Nancy seeks additional RM168mil for welfare
items.summary: KUCHING: The Women, Family and Community Development Ministry has proposed an additional RM168 million under the 2027 Budget to strengthen welfare support for target groups, including the care sector. Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said the proposal included additional support for caregivers of the elderly, many of whom provided unpaid care at home. "The ministry has proposed a total welfare allocation of nearly RM4 billion, including about RM3 billion for existing welfare recipients, while the additional allocation includes measures to strengthen the care sector," she told a press conference after launching the Care Sector Initiative under the Madani 2026 Budget here today.

items.title: Zahid, Fadillah urge Muslims to embody Prophet's values
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Maulidur Rasul should be observed by commemorating the birth of Prophet Muhammad and emulating his sirah, character and Sunnah as guidance in all aspects of life, says Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi. In a Facebook post, he expressed hope that Maulidur Rasul 1448H would continue to nurture Muslims' love for the Prophet, strengthen brotherhood and inspire them to contribute to society. Meanwhile, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof said Maulidur Rasul was not merely about recalling the Prophet's life or reciting selawat, but about embodying his Sunnah and character in daily life.

items.title: Police chase uncovers 442kg of cooking oil in MPV
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU: A police chase involving a suspicious vehicle in Chalok, Setiu, led to the discovery of 442kg of 1kg packets of cooking oil in a Nissan Grand Livina. Terengganu Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry (KPDN) director Mohd Mufsi Lat said the Hulu Terengganu KPDN branch received the case from the police following the discovery. He said the incident began when police spotted a suspicious vehicle and gave chase before it crashed.

items.title: Five main Kajang roads to close from Wednesday for Merdeka eve
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Five main roads around Kajang will be closed in stages from Wednesday and fully closed on Aug 30 for the 2026 Selangor State Merdeka Eve Celebration at Kajang Stadium. Kajang police chief Assistant Commissioner Naazron Abdul Yusof said the closures were aimed at ensuring smooth traffic flow and public safety during the celebration. He said Jalan Mahkamah would be fully closed from Aug 26 to 30, while Jalan Cempaka Putih, Jalan Cempaka Kuning, Jalan Stadium and Jalan Cheras would be closed in stages.

items.title: High Court dismisses Negeri Sembilan state government’s bid to evict Undangs from official halls, residences
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 24 —The High Court here today dismissed two applications by the Negeri Sembilan government seeking an immediate eviction involving the official halls and residences of the Undang of Rembau and Undang of Sungei Ujong. Judge Roz Mawar Rozain ruled through an online proceeding that the state government lacked legal standing (locus standi) to initiate the proceedings under Order 89 of the Rules of Court. The court ruled that the disputed premises are classified as reserved land under the National Land Code (NLC), rather than ordinary state land.

items.title: Man jailed three months, fined RM400 for impersonating MACC officer
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 24 —An unemployed man was sentenced to three months' jail and fined RM400 in the Selayang Magistrate's Court here today after pleading guilty to impersonating a Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) officer. Mohd Izham Mohd Zainuddin, 34, received the sentence from Magistrate Chai Guan Hock and was ordered to start his jail term from the date of arrest on July 30, 2026. The court also ordered the accused to be sentenced for a month if he failed to pay his fine.

items.title: PM Anwar inaugurates Malaysia’s latest film landmark
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 24 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today officially opened the National Film Development Corporation Malaysia (Finas) Tower in Damansara, marking a new phase in strengthening Malaysia’s film and audiovisual industry under the Orange Economy framework. Prime minister Anwar Ibrahim said the new Finas Tower marks a new chapter in strengthening Malaysia’s film and audiovisual industry as part of the Orange Economy. Communications and Multimedia Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said Menara Finas, developed on a 5.14-acre site, began construction on January 20, 2021, and has now become the country’s new film industry hub.

items.title: Shoplot housing Village Park restaurant in Uptown Damansara set for RM5.3m auction
items.summary: A court document sighted by Malay Mail shows that the three-and-a-half-storey intermediate shopoffice at No. The document also states Standard Chartered Bank Malaysia Berhad's mortgage issuance date for the property is November 20, 2012. As for the auction, it was ordered by the High Court in Kuala Lumpur, with the document citing court orders dated January 8 and July 23 this year.

items.title: High Court dismisses bid to forfeit RM21m, gold bar seized from Aman Palestin
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 24 — The High Court here today dismissed the prosecution’s application to forfeit funds amounting to RM21 million, including foreign currency totaling US$139,650.68, which had been frozen under the name of the company Aman Palestin Berhad (Aman Palestin). The forfeiture application also involved a one-kilogram gold bar that was previously seized. Judge Datuk Seri Latifah Mohd Tahar, who is now a Court of Appeal Judge, made the decision after examining and listening to the written and oral submissions from both the prosecution and the respondent, Aman Palestin.

items.title: Penang enforces Private Accommodation By‑Laws, vows crackdown on unlicensed short‑term rentals
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 24 — The enforcement of the Private Accommodation By-Laws 2026 marks a crucial step in ensuring that short-term accommodation operators run their businesses legally and in compliance with regulations. President of the Malaysian Budget and Business Hotel Association (MyBHA), Dr Sri Ganesh Michiel, said the move is also vital to protect the safety of residents and tourists, while ensuring fairness and legal compliance. Penang became the first state in the country to enforce the Private Accommodation By-Laws effective Aug 1, to strengthen the regulation and enforcement of private accommodation operations.

items.title: Twins Serene and Irene Lock clinch top honours at Malaysia’s BEM Engineering Awards
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 24 — Identical twins Dr Serene Lock Sow Mun and Irene Lock Sow Mei, 36, who have shared a classroom since primary school, achieved national recognition after being named among Malaysia’s top engineers at the Board of Engineers Malaysia (BEM) Engineering Awards ceremony last night. Sow Mun, an associate professor at Universiti Teknologi Petronas (UTP) became the first woman to win the National Young Engineer Award, while her sister Sow Mei, a senior process engineer at Petronas, received the Special Mention International Engineering Award (SMIEA) 2026. This recognition motivates me to contribute even more to the engineering field,” Sow Mei told Bernama.

items.title: MetMalaysia warns of evening storms across peninsula, Sabah, Sarawak
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 24 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm warning for parts of eight states and territories, warning residents to brace for heavy downpours, strong winds, and lightning strikes until 6:00pm today. According to the advisory issued at 3:55pm, severe convective weather is expected across several districts in Peninsular Malaysia, Sarawak, and Sabah. In Peninsular Malaysia, the warning covers Kulim, Baling, and Sik in Kedah, alongside Jeli and Gua Musang in Kelantan.

items.title: Malaysia Airlines retimes KLIA flights as airspace closes for National Day flypast rehearsals
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 24 — Malaysia Airlines Bhd will retime selected flights arriving at and departing from KL International Airport (KLIA) Terminal 1 following temporary airspace closures in conjunction with the 69th National Day celebrations. The national airline said the temporary closures within the Kuala Lumpur Terminal Control Area are to facilitate rehearsals and the National Day Flypast 2026, resulting in scheduled aircraft take-offs and landings at KLIA being temporarily suspended during selected periods. Malaysia Airlines also reminded passengers that check-in counters close 60 minutes before scheduled departure for both domestic and international flights, while boarding gates close 30 minutes before departure.

items.title: Ex-Sabah women and children’s hospital director sues successor, top official over removal
items.summary: Dr Yogendra Panchalingam filed the suit at the High Court of Sabah and Sarawak in Kota Kinabalu on August 21. He named Sabah Health Department deputy director Datuk Dr Abd Kahar Abd Asis and his former deputy turned successor, Dr Christine Lu Shin Yeen, as defendants. Appointed as hospital director in March 2025, Dr Yogendra denied all allegations of sexual harassment levelled against him, including complaints lodged by Dr Lu and the hospital’s corporate communications unit head, Elleyvianna Murang.

items.title: Zara Qairina inquest hears olive‑green ‘Love And Peace’ journal altered, 64 sheets missing
items.summary: The 77th witness, forensic science lecturer and researcher from Universiti Sains Malaysia (USM) Dr Wan Nur Syuhaila Mat Desa, said the journals comprised a green journal marked W1, a pastel purple “Simple Style Book” journal (W2), a dark brown journal (W3) and an olive-green “Love And Peace” journal (WK9). Meanwhile, W2 contained only 53 sheets compared with 96 sheets in a new reference journal, meaning 43 sheets were missing, while W3 contained 77 sheets against 98 sheets in the reference journal, leaving 21 sheets missing. She said WK9 was received in worn and torn condition and contained only 54 sheets compared with 118 sheets in a new reference journal of the same type, meaning 64 sheets were missing.

items.title: Police tighten Malaysia–Thailand border security after Yala, Pattani, Narathiwat blasts
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 24 — Police have stepped up security preparedness at the Malaysia-Thailand border following a series of explosions and attacks in Yala, Pattani and Narathiwat, southern Thailand, with the areas remaining under control. He said PDRM was also strengthening its prevention, early detection and rapid response approaches, as well as increasing intelligence and information sharing with Thai security agencies. Mohd Yusri said so far there were no reports of Malaysians being affected in the incident.

items.title: Malaysia, Indonesia to synchronise haze suppression ops as monsoon and El Niño converge
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 24 — Malaysia and Indonesia have agreed to ramp up preventive measures to tackle cross-border haze, to safeguard air quality, especially in the lead-up to the National Day and Malaysia Day celebrations. Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability (NRES) Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said the commitment was reached during a phone call today with his Indonesian counterpart, Environment Minister Jumhur Hidayat. The 69th National Day celebration is set to take place at Dataran Putrajaya on Aug 31, while the Malaysia Day celebration will be held in Kuching, Sarawak, on Sept 16.

items.title: Finas moves to combat ‘cartels’ and ensure fair competition in local film market
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 24 — The National Film Development Corporation Malaysia (Finas) is moving to convene industry players to address alleged distribution monopolies and ensure fair competition within the local cinematic market. Chief executive officer Datuk Azmir Saifuddin Mutalib acknowledged growing anxiety over the concentration of control in film distribution, specifically where a single entity dominates production, funding, and distribution. We want fair trade and opportunities for all industry players,” Azmir told reporters at the new Menara Finas headquarters in Damansara Damai.

items.title: Economy minister: Tabung Haji’s RM96b investments make governance crucial to market confidence
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 24 — The government has cast the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) findings on Tabung Haji’s management between 2014 and 2020 as part of a wider push to tighten governance, strengthen accountability and restore public confidence in national institutions. From an economic perspective, he noted, Tabung Haji’s governance is crucial given its scale and role. “With investments exceeding RM96 billion, Tabung Haji’s governance has wider implications for confidence in institutions and the domestic market.

items.title: KTMB rolls out special timetable, adds trains for northern routes during school holidays and Merdeka
items.summary: It added that the move would increase the total number of services on the Butterworth-Padang Besar-Butterworth route from 38 to 46 services per day. “Of the total, four additional services will be provided for the Padang Besar-Butterworth route, taking the total to 23 services per day compared with 19 services under the regular timetable. “Four additional services will also be provided for the Butterworth-Padang Besar route, bringing the total to 23 services per day,” it added.

items.title: Tahfiz teacher in Ampang pleads not guilty to four sexual assault charges on pupils
items.summary: The accused, Muhammad Ilyas Jamaludin, is alleged to have committed the offences against the two boys, aged 10 and 11, at the premises between July and August 2026. The charges were preferred under Sections 14(a) and 14(b) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017, and read together with Section 16(1) of the same Act. Under Section 14(a) and 14(b), the offence carries a maximum penalty of 20 years’ imprisonment and caning and Section 16(1) provides for an additional term of up to five years’ imprisonment and no fewer than two strokes of the cane, upon conviction.

items.title: IGP urges Malaysians to reduce travel to southern Thailand amid tense security
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 24 — Police have stepped up security along the Malaysia-Thailand border following more than 50 bombings, arson attacks on local government offices and tyre-burning reported in three provinces of southern Thailand last Saturday. Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail also urged the public to stay away from the conflict zones, citing safety concerns amid the escalating tension. Earlier at the ceremony, Mohd Khalid received the Darjah Gemilang Seri Melaka (D.G.S.M.)

items.title: Sabah Electricity confirms fatal electrocution during pole replacement works in Sandakan, one injured
items.summary: SANDAKAN, Aug 24 — A worker was electrocuted during installation works on an electric pole at Bandar Tabin Jaya, here on Saturday. “Personnel from the Sabah Electricity helped disconnect the electricity before the man was brought down using special equipment,” he said in a statement. Meanwhile, Sabah Electricity Sdn Bhd (Sabah Electricity) has confirmed the incident involving two contractor workers during electrical pole replacement works near the traffic light junction leading to Taman Mawar here, on Aug 22.

items.title: Roller coaster mishap at Subang Jaya theme park leaves ten hurt, police investigating
items.summary: SUBANG JAYA, Aug 24 — Ten people sustained minor injuries in a roller coaster incident at a theme park here. District police chief ACP Wan Azlan Wan Mamat said the incident took place at about 9pm on Saturday, while the report was lodged with police at 11.45am yesterday. “Anyone with information can contact the Subang Jaya Police headquarters at 03-78627100,” he said.

items.title: PM Anwar to deliver National Day ‘Amanat Perdana’ at Dataran Merdeka
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 24 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim will deliver the 2026 National Day ‘Amanat Perdana’ on Aug 30 to convey the aspirations and hopes of the Madani Government leadership on the importance of embracing the spirit of independence and fostering patriotism among Malaysians. Organised by the National Unity Ministry, the event will be held at Dataran Merdeka, with various programmes starting as early as 5pm, including the Merdeka Eve Animation Concert, World Festival of Lights, Gema Perpaduan Malaysia Madani cultural performance, a special Independence Musical segment and performances by leading local artistes. National Unity Minister Datuk Aaron Ago Dagang said the well-being that the country aspires to enjoy could not be achieved without strong unity.

items.title: Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek among top honourees at Melaka’s state awards
items.summary: Fadhlina received the Darjah Gemilang Seri Melaka (D.G.S.M) which carries the title of Datuk Seri. Also receiving the same title were Chief Justice of Malaya Datuk Seri Hashim Hamzah, Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail and Chief Commissioner of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman. Meanwhile, 56 individuals received the Darjah Cemerlang Seri Melaka (D.C.S.M) award which carries the title of Datuk Wira, including Benut assemblyman Datuk Mohd Sumali Reduan, Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department director Datuk M. Kumar, National Solid Waste Management Department director-general Datuk Dr Mohd Azhar Abd Hamid and Melaka police chief Datuk Dzulkhairi Mukhtar.

items.title: Linkedua shutdown: Eight including motoring influencer held after staging illegal race on Malaysia-Singapore link
items.summary: KULAI, Aug 24 — A motoring influencer was among eight local men remanded for four days to assist investigations into a case involving the closure of a section of the Malaysia-Singapore Second Link (Linkedua) to stage an illegal race last Saturday. The remand order, effective today until Thursday (Aug 27), was issued by Magistrate R. Salini after police applied for the order at the Kulai Magistrate’s Court to assist investigations under Section 42(1) of the Road Transport Act (RTA) 1987. Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad was reported to have said that the group was believed to have blocked the road from KM33 at the Senai Utara Toll interchange to KM31 at the Johor Premium Outlet (JPO) interchange on Linkedua to stage an illegal race.

items.title: Penang land sale probe: MACC extends remand for agency chief and company director
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 24 — The remand period for a government agency chairman and a company director has been extended for another three days until Wednesday to assist investigations into an abuse of power case involving the disposal of land in Penang, with losses estimated at RM1.96 million. On Thursday, five people, comprising a government agency chairman, two company directors, a technical manager and a female clerk, were detained at the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) office. The chairman is suspected of abusing his position while serving as deputy chairman and a member of the Board of Directors to approve the sale of eight plots of land belonging to an agency under a ministry in Seberang Perai Selatan in 2015.

items.title: FMM dismisses MTUC’s RM3,100 minimum wage proposal as unrealistic for businesses
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 24 — The Federation of Malaysian Manufacturers (FMM) has rejected a proposal by the Malaysian Trades Union Congress (MTUC) to raise the national minimum wage from RM1,700 to RM3,100, cautioning that an 82.4 per cent surge is detached from prevailing economic realities. FMM president Jacob Lee Chor Kok said that while the federation supports higher wages as Malaysia strives for high-income status, an abrupt RM1,400 increase in a single revision remains unprecedented. Under the National Wages Consultative Council (NWCC) Act, the next mandatory statutory wage review is slated for February 2027.

items.title: E-hailing driver charged with attempted murder after setting woman on fire in Kepong
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 24 — An e-hailing driver has claimed trial at the Sessions Court here to an attempted murder charge after allegedly dousing a 62-year-old woman in petrol and setting her ablaze in Kepong earlier this month. Ang Kam Tong, 58, pleaded not guilty after the charge was read before Judge Surita Budin, FMT reported. Deputy Public Prosecutor Nur Shakila Shariff objected to bail, telling the court that Ang had attempted to evade arrest.

items.title: Court of Appeal dismisses Indira Gandhi’s RM100m suit despite flagging police shortcomings
items.summary: While dismissing the appeal, a three-member bench chaired by Datuk Mohamed Zaini Mazlan highlighted material deficiencies in police records concerning efforts to execute an arrest warrant against her fugitive former husband, K. Pathmanathan, also known as Muhammad Riduan Abdullah, NST reported. Datuk Faizah Jamaludin and Datuk Mohd Radzi Abdul Hamid also sat on the bench. Delivering the unanimous decision, Faizah ruled that the available evidence failed to establish that any specific police omission directly prevented Pathmanathan’s arrest or the recovery of Prasana.

items.title: Sarawak leads haze misery as Serian hits 194, unhealthy API spreads to Selangor, Kedah, Penang
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 24 — Ten areas in four states recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 10am today, with Serian, Sarawak recording the highest reading, nearing the very unhealthy level. Other areas in the state that recorded unhealthy air quality were Kuching (176), Samarahan (172), Sri Aman (158) and Bintulu (125). A further 58 areas nationwide recorded moderate air quality.

items.title: Three squatter homes razed in Sentul blaze, 26‑year‑old man treated for burn injuries
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 24 — A man suffered burns to his body and legs in a fire that destroyed three squatter houses in Jalan Ismail Ghani, Kampung Kasipillay, Sentul, here early this morning. Kuala Lumpur Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) operations assistant director Ahmad Mukhlis Mukhtar said the emergency call was received at 1.15am before teams from Sentul, Hang Tuah and Gombak Selatan Fire and Rescue Stations rushed to the location. “Upon arrival of the fire brigade at the location, the fire was found to involve three semi-permanent squatter houses with a total area of 4,872 square feet.
